acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_exceed_cumulative
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocol), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged), AND (c) candidate successes > cumulative successes pooled over the same cells on the same cohort (strictly exceed; candidate_successes >= cumulative_successes + 1). Sub-condition (c) is this cycle's headline test, per the selected limitation's measurable form: the preceding candidate trailed cumulative by 35 / 48 successes; a less sparse gate that still trails plain cumulative retention has not answered the limitation, whatever its other scores.

acceptance_criteria.name: recovery_engagement_materially_higher_and_selective
acceptance_criteria.rule: Graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY (no TEST outcomes), per cohort: (a) the recovery branch fires (joint_count >= 1, acting source retained_archive) in at least 4 of the 6 return-A onset seed-checkpoint states (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds) - materially more than the preceding candidate's 1 of 6 on both of its cohorts, and at the low edge of this protocol's design interval of approx 4-5 of 6; AND (b) the recovery branch fires in at most 1 of the 6 B1 onset seed-checkpoint states (at B1 no reversed-rule knowledge is retained and the archive and reference majorities agree, so systematic B1 engagement is false recovery). B2 and control engagement counts are reported, not graded under this criterion (B2 non-recovery is a pre-registered expectation - see expected failure modes - and control engagement is graded downstream under criterion 6).

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Recovery must not buy its return-A successes with harm elsewhere: false recovery at B1/B2 or noisy archive play that pushes pooled onset harm above the abstaining guard's level FAILs this criterion. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded. (See budgets.harm_budget for why the preceding protocol's pooled 75-percent-of-recent8 sub-condition is not carried over, and criterion 4 for the return-A-specific ceiling that is.)

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. Carried over unchanged from the preceding protocol: on prior cohorts frozen_A's and cumulative's return-A harm (30-38 pooled) shows the 60-percent level (approx 44-50) is attainable when retained knowledge actually engages; a candidate engaging at 4+ of 6 states should approach it, and archive play's own nonzero harm (design approx 4-8 per firing state) is the cost counted against it.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 4 and the preceding candidate's criterion 5: the recovery branch must not break release, and productivity must not collapse toward the always-abstain control.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_downstream_selectivity
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 5 and the preceding candidate's criterion 6. Recovery engagement on stationary evidence is expected at a design approx 2-4 of 15 graded states (reference-majority sampling errors manufacture joint events there) and is NOT itself a failure - the archive model is a valid stationary model - but its downstream totals must stay within these bounds.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, joint_count, opposed_count, matched_count, concordant_count, archive_matched_count, branch taken, recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule alone
baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criterion 1 comparison
baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. The decisive comparator for this experiment: plain cumulative retention, with no signal machinery at all, dominated the preceding candidate at return-A (58 / 66 pooled successes vs its 23 / 18) and triggered its grading cap. Criterion 1 sub-condition (c) holds the candidate to EXCEEDING cumulative on the same cohort - the campaign's selected measurable form for this cycle.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; engagement and return-A comparisons in the report (not a PASS/FAIL comparator in the criteria, whose floors are absolute or against cumulative/frozen_A/guard as named)
baselines.name: evidence_opposition_retained_recovery
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Failed): identical acting model, identical immediate signal, identical archive, identical recovery model, differing ONLY in the recovery test (pooled concordant_count == 2 AND opposed_count >= 1). This is the decisive gate comparison: candidate-vs-preceding-candidate differences isolate the joint concordance test alone.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons
baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory (graded Demonstrated): the candidate's own immediate signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response. Criterion 3 and 4 hold the candidate to the guard's harm levels on the same cohort.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criterion 1 comparison
baselines.name: frozen_A
baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated. The recovery target reference at return_A: what pure retained pre-switch knowledge scores there.

baselines.name: recent32
baselines.role: Relation model on the last 32 observed events.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; preceding-learner comparison
baselines.name: gated_archive_prequential
baselines.role: GatedArchivePrequentialMemory (graded Failed / regression): the earlier archive-routing candidate.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; productivity floor reference
baselines.name: always_abstain
baselines.role: Abstains on every TEST task: 0 successes, 0 harmful actions, all tasks failed-by-abstention. The trivially safe control.

baselines.name: untrained_random
baselines.role: Independent seeded random TEST action policy; gathers no training outcomes.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint, labeled privileged
baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle
baselines.role: PRIVILEGED reference only: knows the expected hidden rule (not the realized stochastic flip). Never a realizable baseline and never counted in any PASS/FAIL comparison.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 6 per stage per cohort at checkpoints 2 and 4.

budgets.abstention_budget: Abstention remains the fallback when a change is detected but no joint return evidence exists. Criteria 5 and 6 bound its downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the graded guard and retained-recovery protocols.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. (The preceding protocol's additional pooled 75-percent-of-recent8 sub-condition is NOT carried over: the campaign's selected measurable form for this cycle specifies the guard-relative bound, and on the preceding cohorts the guard itself - the demonstrated harm standard - pooled at 97 / 93 percent of recent8 because its abstention branch was nearly silent there, so a fixed 75-percent pooled ceiling grades abstention-branch luck on B1/B2, which this recovery mechanism does not act on, rather than recovery behavior at return-A. The return-A-specific 60-percent ceiling in criterion 4, where recovery DOES act, is carried over unchanged.)
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Exceed-cumulative shortfall (pre-registered as the central risk): engagement succeeds (criterion 2 passes) but pooled return-A successes still trail cumulative, because cumulative acts with a near-frozen_A model at EVERY return-A state while the candidate forfeits approx 6-8 successes at each non-engaging state and gains little per engaging state (archive and cumulative models are close). Criteria 1 FAILs on sub-condition (c) even though the gate change worked as designed - the honest finding would then be that no signal gate on this recovery model beats plain cumulative retention at a first return in this simulator.

Reference-majority disagreement is more common than design: the reference window is only 24 events (~2-4 per span), so its span majorities may disagree with the archive's on more spans than the assumed 0.15-0.25 - at B1 that directly manufactures joint events (flip-back event on a flipped-majority span), pushing B1 false recovery above 1 of 6 states and failing criteria 2b and 3.

Engagement still below the material floor: if reference majorities at return-A are reversed for fewer spans than design (sparse spans, ties giving null expectations, neutral newest events), per-event joint probability falls toward 0.3 and engagement toward 2-3 of 6 states - better than 1 of 6 but below criterion 2a's floor of 4, and criterion 1 fails with it.

opposed_count == 0 return-A states remain unreachable by design: the joint test requires opposition on the joint event itself, so a return-A state whose newest events happen to agree with the (already partly slid) reference window cannot recover even if both are archive-concordant. This blind spot, recorded as secondary in the preceding experiment, is deliberately NOT the selected limitation here and is reported from the records, not graded away.

Recovery harm is nonzero by construction: archive play in a firing state causes inspected-rate harm approx 4-8 per 16 episodes; a false-recovery cluster at B1/B2 (full-harm states) or a worse archive model on new cohorts pushes pooled onset harm above the guard's level and fails criterion 3, or return-A harm above its ceiling and fails criterion 4.

Stationary joint engagement: on the control arm, reference-majority sampling errors manufacture joint events at a design approx 2-4 of 15 graded states. In this simulator the archive model is itself a good stationary model, so the expected downstream cost is low, but every such engagement is recorded and criterion 6 grades the downstream totals, not the intention.

Persistence interaction at checkpoints 8/16: recovery or abstention may keep engaging while the reference window slides, forfeiting or altering recent8's by-then adaptation; reported in full at 8/16 and graded only as the checkpoint-32 release bound in criterion 5.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard and the graded retained-recovery candidate.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded retained-recovery candidate: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are still recorded in full. What changes is only how the recovery branch USES the per-event flags (see joint_concordance_test). Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive). (2) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2, abstain (choose returns None), exactly the graded guard's protective response when a change is detected but no retained knowledge jointly concords with the newest evidence. (3) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Recovery requires direct per-event evidence of a return: at least one newest event that the retained archive predicts correctly AND the immediate (pre-return) evidence predicts incorrectly. That conjunction on a single event is the return signature. Pooling the two counts across events (the preceding candidate) both dilutes it - two half-signatures on different events could satisfy pooled sub-conditions - and sparsifies it, by requiring the concordance half to appear twice. Abstention retains priority over recent8 acting whenever a change is detected (opposed_count == 2) and no joint return evidence exists.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded evidence-opposition guard and the graded retained-recovery candidate, reused unchanged and not re-tuned: newest window = last 2 observed events; reference window = the 24 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-26 .. N-3). For each newest event, the reference expectation is the strictly-highest reported outcome class among reference events of equal span (tie or empty gives null); an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different. opposed_count in 0..2. No fitted probabilities anywhere in either signal.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: NEW, the single changed element of this experiment. For each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT (per the unchanged archive test above) AND reference-OPPOSED (per the unchanged immediate signal above) - both flags on the SAME event. joint_count is the number of joint newest events (0..2). No other combination of the pooled counts enters the recovery branch: in particular concordant_count >= 1 pooled with opposed_count >= 1 on DIFFERENT events does NOT trigger recovery, and the preceding candidate's concordant_count == 2 AND opposed_count >= 1 rule is not retained as an alternative trigger.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: Both signals together require a 2-event newest window, a full 24-event reference window, and at least 1 archive event: at least 27 observed events. Below 27 events neither signal is evaluable and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so this fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery candidate: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose). The recovery model never includes the reference window or the newest window. Holding the recovery model fixed isolates the concordance test as the only changed variable against the preceding candidate.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery candidate: every observed event BEFORE the reference window, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. It is not a snapshot, not phase-segmented, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates and the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). Per newest event at a return-A onset: the archive holds ~280 events (~28 per span band), so its span majorities are the original rule's class with probability near 1; the reference window holds 24 reversed-rule events (~2-4 per span), so its span majority is the reversed class with design probability approx 0.75-0.85 (majority of 2-4 samples each agreeing with the reversed class at the composed agreement rate approx 0.84 after the 0.1625 disagreement rate from 1/8 stochastic + 1/20 report flips), tied/null or original otherwise. A newest return event is archive-concordant with design probability approx 0.65-0.70 (the preceding protocol's derivation: non-neutral span fraction approx 0.8 x agreement approx 0.84) and, conditional on concordance, is opposed whenever its span's reference majority is reversed, so per-event joint probability is approx 0.45-0.55. Recovery engages per state with probability 1 - (1 - p_joint)^2 approx 0.70-0.80, i.e. approx 4-5 of 6 return-A onset states per cohort - hence criterion 2's engagement floor at 4 of 6, set at the low edge of the design interval to allow binomial noise across only 6 states. At a B1 onset the archive and reference majorities are BOTH the original rule (the archive is pre-switch evidence; the reference window is the pre-switch tail): a joint event requires a span where the reference majority disagrees with the archive majority (reference sampling error, design approx 0.15-0.25 per span) AND a newest event following the archive side - but B1 newest events follow the REVERSED rule, so following the archive side means a flip-back event (per-event concordance at B1 approx 0.25-0.33 per the preceding protocol, and only the subset of those whose span's reference majority is also flipped counts): per-event joint probability approx 0.05-0.08, per-state engagement approx 0.10-0.15, expected B1 firing approx 0.6-0.9 of 6 states - hence criterion 2's B1 ceiling of at most 1 of 6 states, a falsifiable bound at the design expectation's upper edge, not a certainty. The same majority-agreement argument applies at B2 onset (reference window is the return-A segment, archive majority still original) and is why B2 recovery is NOT expected. On stationary evidence the majorities also agree, but newest events follow the archive rule at the full concordant rate (approx 0.65), so per-event joint probability is approx 0.10-0.16 and recovery may engage at roughly 2-4 of the 15 graded control states; the archive model is itself a valid stationary model there, so - exactly as in the preceding protocol - engagement on the control arm is recorded and its downstream totals are graded under criterion 6, not the engagement count itself. Success arithmetic, stated honestly in advance: if recovery engages at 4-5 of 6 return-A states at archive-model rates (the preceding candidate's two firing states scored 9 and 11 successes per 16 episodes; frozen_A pooled approx 10.7-11 per state on prior cohorts) and the remaining states act as recent8/guard (approx 2-4 successes per state at return-A onset), the candidate's pooled return-A successes land approx 44-58, while cumulative pooled 58-66 on the preceding cohorts (within 0-6 of frozen_A). Criterion 1's exceed-cumulative sub-condition is therefore set DELIBERATELY at the campaign's selected measurable form, above this protocol's central design expectation: passing it requires engagement at 6 of 6 states, or archive-model per-state rates above cumulative's, or a new-cohort cumulative at the low end of its prior range. That is the registered question - whether a less sparse test can beat plain cumulative retention - and a FAIL on it is an informative, pre-registered outcome, not a protocol defect to be repaired after seeing scores. Criterion 1's other floors (40 percent of frozen_A; guard + 16) are carried over unchanged from the preceding protocol for continuity.

candidate.name: JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory and the graded EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

capability_under_test: Recovery engagement without loss of selectivity at a return to a previously learned rule: whether a recovery rule whose concordance test is less sparse - a per-event JOINT test, requiring at least one newest event that is simultaneously archive-concordant (agrees with the retained archive's span majority) and reference-opposed (disagrees with the immediate reference window's span majority) - can, at return_A checkpoints 2 and 4, engage at materially more onset states than the preceding pooled both-events test (1 of 6 per cohort), exceed plain cumulative retention's return-A successes, keep false recovery at B1 at or below 1 of 6 states, and keep pooled onset harm at or below the evidence-opposition guard's level on the same cohort. Priority 1 items 2 + 3 joined to item 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge and first-contact overconfidence.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 are the graded recovery window for return_A and the graded onset window for harm; 8 and 16 report persistence costs; 32 grades release. return_A has 48 TRAIN events and the control continuation 64, so 32 is within range for every arm. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world (and by the decision rule recovery cannot engage at k=0 of B1/B2, where the newest events are pre-switch).

grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit. No separate cumulative-dominance cap is needed in this protocol: criterion 1 sub-condition (c) already requires exceeding cumulative, so the preceding protocol's cap is subsumed by a graded criterion.
grading.failed: Any of criteria 1-4 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, and routing rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint test, and decision rule are all designer-supplied. A PASS would demonstrate less-sparse signal-gated recovery of retained knowledge at a first return in this simulator only, not general regime identification (the archive is global and unsegmented; B2 recovery is pre-registered as not expected), not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criteria 1, 3, and 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 2, 4, 5, or 6 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.

hypothesis: The preceding candidate pooled its two counts across the newest window: it required BOTH newest events archive-concordant (concordant_count == 2) plus at least one opposed anywhere in the window, so the concordance and opposition evidence could come from different events while a single event carrying both signatures counted for only half the requirement. At a genuine return the two signatures are not independent pieces of evidence spread across events - they are two views of the SAME event: a post-return event agrees with the retained archive's majority (built from ~280 events, original-rule dominated, reliable per span) and disagrees with the immediate reference window's majority (the reversed-rule segment). Requiring both flags on one event and at least one such joint event in the window removes the squaring that made the pooled test sparse (design per-state engagement approx 0.70-0.80, vs the pooled test's realized 1 of 6), while keeping selectivity where it matters: at a B1 onset (and at B2, and on stationary evidence) the archive and reference majorities AGREE with each other, so a joint event additionally requires a span where the two majorities disagree - a reference sampling error - compounded with an event that follows the archive side, a compound event with design probability approx 0.05-0.13 per newest event at B1 against approx 0.45-0.55 at a return. A single concordant event ALONE was correctly rejected by the preceding protocol as consistent with flip-back noise (per-event concordance at B1 approx 0.25-0.33); a single JOINT event is a different, much more specific observation, and this experiment tests whether that specificity is real.
limitation_evidence: EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_RETAINED_RECOVERY (docs/EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_RETAINED_RECOVERY.md, graded Failed 2026-10-30, cohorts 322003-family / 323001-family now INSPECTED): criteria 1-4 FAIL on both cohorts, cumulative-dominance cap triggered on both. The recovery branch fired at exactly 1 of 6 return-A onset states per cohort; concordant_count == 1 in 5 of 6 return-A onset states in BOTH cohorts - one newest event archive-concordant, the other not - so the both-events requirement (concordant_count == 2) was the binding constraint, the protocol's own pre-registered failure mode 1. Candidate pooled return-A onset successes 23 / 18 at harm 73 / 78, against frozen_A 64 / 66, cumulative 58 / 66 at harm 38 / 30, and the guard 14 / 13.

Same experiment, mechanism evidence: where recovery did fire it converted as designed (additional firing state 11 successes / 5 harm vs recent8 6 / 10 in that state; development firing state 9 successes where the guard abstained, harm 7 = recent8 there), and false recovery at B1 never occurred (0 of 6 states, both cohorts). The gate was selective; its sensitivity failed. The retained knowledge itself is not the problem: frozen_A and cumulative both score 58-66 pooled return-A onset successes at harm 30-38 on those cohorts.

Same experiment, pooled onset harm: candidate 262 (development, identical to recent8 in all six onset cells) and 231 (additional) vs the guard's 255 / 236 and recent8's 262 / 254. On cohorts where the abstention branch is nearly silent, pooled onset harm is dominated by unprotected recent8 acting in non-engaging states - engagement sparsity, not recovery harm, is what keeps pooled harm at recent8's level.

EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD (docs/EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD.md, graded Demonstrated 2026-10-29, cohorts 312003-family / 313001-family now INSPECTED): the evidence-count onset signal itself separates onsets from stationary noise (all six criteria PASS on both cohorts); detection exists - what has failed twice since is the response to it at a return (abstention forfeits retained knowledge; pooled both-events recovery engages too rarely to inherit it).
Handoff section 8 standing limitations: slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge remains a listed persistent weakness.
metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.

Candidate decision record at every checkpoint, per seed: the immediate signal record exactly as in the graded guard protocol (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, reference event count, reference majority class or null, matched flag, opposed flag; plus opposed_count, matched_count), the archive concordance record exactly as in the graded retained-recovery protocol (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, archive event count for that span, archive majority class or null, archive-matched flag, archive-concordant flag; plus concordant_count, archive_matched_count), the per-event JOINT flag (archive-concordant AND reference-opposed, same event) and joint_count, the branch taken (retained_archive / abstained / recent8 / all_available_below_minimum), recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, and the acting source.

Recovery engagement aggregates per cohort, from the decision records alone: recovery-fired states, abstention states, and recent8 states among the 6 return-A onset states, the 6 B1 onset states, the 6 B2 onset states, and the graded control states; plus, for continuity with the preceding experiment, the states at which the preceding candidate's pooled rule (concordant_count == 2 AND opposed_count >= 1) would have fired, computed from this candidate's recorded counts (the counts are recorded in full, so this is a records-only derivation, not a re-run).
Onset harm and successes at checkpoint 0 for every stage, per seed and method, reported explicitly as a diagnostic and never pooled into any graded onset figure and never hidden.
Persistence cost: candidate abstentions, recovery engagements, successes, and harm at checkpoints 8 and 16 per stage, reported alongside the checkpoint-32 release figures.
Per seed TRAIN accounting, counted once regardless of checkpoints or methods: actor actions, actual harmful actions, actual productive, actual neutral, reported harmful, report label flips.
Learner-issued information-acquisition actions (frozen at 0) and any additional observations requested (frozen at 0).
Checkpoint record SHA256 and restore-replay identity for the candidate.
No pooled-only reporting: every cohort figure must be decomposable into its three per-seed rows, and every pooled criterion figure into its per-cell rows.
permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its recovery model, or its checkpoint record.
priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4. This experiment builds directly on the graded retained-recovery failure: the recovery mechanism converted where it engaged and never false-fired at B1, but its pooled both-events concordance test engaged at only 1 of 6 return-A onset states per cohort, so plain cumulative retention dominated it. This cycle changes exactly one thing - where the concordance and opposition evidence must sit (on the SAME newest event, jointly) - and asks whether the less sparse test engages materially more, beats cumulative at return-A, and stays selective at B1.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the four graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the immediate opposition signal, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the recovery model, the abstention branch, and every window size are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the retained-recovery protocol (newest window 2, reference window 24, archive events[:N-26], opposed_count and concordant_count definitions unchanged). The single new element - the per-event joint flag and the joint_count >= 1 recovery threshold - is derived a priori from the structure of the two majorities and the simulator's known noise rates (1/8 stochastic flips, 1/20 report flips), as derived in candidate.fixed_parameters.threshold_justification, informed only by the preceding experiment's published graded aggregates (its limitation evidence), never by any score of this experiment (none exist).
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures recovery-branch selectivity: false engagement, false abstention, and lost productivity when nothing changed.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)
